newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault up with market despite warning.
newsitem.headline: Renault up with market despite warning.

text.p: Renault shares rose in a stronger French stock market despite a warning of bigger losses than previously expected for 1996 from its commercial vehicles division.
The share rose around 2.5 percent before easing back to stand 1.75 percent up at 122.2 francs at 1014 GMT, while the CAC 40 leading share index was up 1.11 percent at the same time.
"The market is of course strong today," said BZW analyst Philip Ayton. The warning on commercial vehicles was more important than nine-month overall sales figures in line with expectations, he said.
Paris bourse traders said, however, that they saw the car sales figures as relatively positive.

The group said earlier on Friday total sales for the third quarter had risen 5.33 percent in the car division to 33.329 billion francs but slipped 10.1 percent in the commercial vehicles division to 6.358 billion from 7.065 billion.

"On the car side, sales were up 5.33 percent but there's nothing good about that because registrations rose 21 percent in the quarter," said another car industry analyst. "That means there's huge price discounting."
He said of the figures "They are poor but not dramatic".

Renault, which had already predicted a negative contribution from commercial vehicles for 1996, said in its sales statement: "the negative contribution from the commercial vehicles division will be considerably more pronounced than anticipated".

"Truck sales are down but not as much as I was expecting," said one analyst, adding that the warning on the 1996 result from this division would not prompt him to change forecasts on the group was a whole.
Ayton said of the car sales figure, "There's very little money being made by carmakers. Renault is facing up to the problem but it remains to be seen if it will be enough."
